hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, वहाँ नक्षत्र आदि अनुकूल होने पर पुण्याह शब्द के साथ, गाय, ब्राह्मण और वृद्धों की प्रदक्षिणा करती हुई प्रवेश करके, बहुत बार प्रसव कर चुकी, अनुक्ताभिः और अविपादाभिः अस्पष्ट, क्लेश सहने वाली स्त्रियों से घिरी हुई, स्वस्त्ययन में लगी हुई, अनुलोमन करने वाले आहार और विहार से वात, मूत्र और मल को अनुलोम की हुई प्रसव के समय की प्रतीक्षा करे।
english: On a conjectural reading: there, when the stars and the rest are favourable, with the utterance of puṇyāha (auspicious-day formula), but circling clockwise round the cows, brahmins and elders, having entered, surrounded by (ones) who have given birth many times, anuktābhiḥ and avipādābhiḥ (unclear), able to bear hardship, devoted to auspicious rites (svastyayana), with wind, urine and stool made to move properly by regulating food and conduct, she should await the time of delivery.

text_flags.why: possible: tu + ā gives 'tvā'; the doubled avagraha mark is a print habit; the sense 'circling round' is not firm.
possible: tr for vr is a common OCR confusion; 'surrounded' fits.
possible: 'nerā' for 'nair ā' (ai printed e), and 'mtra' for 'mūtra' (ū lost); the sense fits.

possible: anuktā ('unsaid') and avipādā (not a known word) give no sense among attendant qualities; anuraktā ('devoted') and avipannā ('unharmed') are conjectured (r and n lost). Kept as printed and unglossed in `words`.

notes: Damaged or unclear print: 'anuktābhiḥ' and 'avipādābhiḥ' are real forms but the sense in a list of qualities of attendants is unclear (they may hide other words); they are kept unglossed. 'prasūtābhir bahuśaḥ' is read as 'by those who have given birth many times'. 'tu' with 'āvartamānā' is awkward and uncertain. The ritual 'puṇyāha' is an auspicious-day benediction. 'pradakṣiṇam' = keeping the right side toward the object. Subject (the woman) is understood; the sentence is long and the join with unit 40 (the chamber) is by context.
lines_deva: तत्रानुकूलेषु नक्षत्रादिषु पुण्याहशब्देन गोब्राह्मणवृद्धान्त्वाऽऽवर्तमाना प्रदक्षिणं प्रविश्यबहुशः प्रसूताभिरनुक्ताभिरविपादाभिः क्लेशक्षमाभिः परितृता स्वस्त्ययनपराऽनुलोमनेराहारविहारैरनुलोमितवातम्त्रपुरीषा प्रसवकालमुदीक्षेत
lines_iast: tatrānukūleṣu nakṣatrādiṣu puṇyāhaśabdena gobrāhmaṇavṛddhāntvā''vartamānā pradakṣiṇaṃ praviśyabahuśaḥ prasūtābhiranuktābhiravipādābhiḥ kleśakṣamābhiḥ paritṛtā svastyayanaparā'nulomanerāhāravihārairanulomitavātamtrapurīṣā prasavakālamudīkṣeta

hindi: और मल तथा मूत्र की थोड़ी सी भी रुकावट में फलवर्तियाँ यानी बत्तियाँ रखे।
english: And even in a slight obstruction (vibandha) of stool and urine, one should insert phalavartis (suppositories).
notes: 'svalpe'pi' is su-alpe api, 'even slight'. 'phalavarti' = a suppository (varti = wick-like roll); the substance 'phala' is not specified here. The text speaks of obstruction of stool and urine (vibandha = constipation / retention). Insertion site and subject are not stated.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., dvandva then tat-puruṣa

hindi: तब जिसका प्रसव निकट है, उसमें थकावट, ग्लानि, मानो बन्धन छूटे हुए दोनों नेत्र, थूक, मूत्र और मल की अधिकता, कुक्षि की शिथिलता, नीचे भारीपन, अन्न में अरुचि, पेट, हृदय, कटि यानी कमर, बस्ति यानी मूत्राशय और वंक्षण यानी जाँघ के जोड़ में पीड़ा; चुभन, फटन, शूल, फड़कन और योनि के स्राव होते हैं।
english: Then, in her whose delivery is near, there occur exhaustion (klama), weariness (glāni), the two eyes as if with released fastenings, abundance of spitting, urine and stool, looseness of the belly, heaviness below, lack of desire for food, pain (vedanā) in the belly (udara), heart (hṛdaya), waist, bladder (basti) and groin; and pricking (toda), tearing (bheda), pain (śūla), throbbing (sphuraṇa) and flows (sravaṇa) of the yoni occur.

text_flags.why: possible: a stray 't' in 'darathṛdaya'; 'udara-hṛdaya' fits.
possible: st for s; sravaṇa 'flow' is the usual word, stravaṇa is not a recognised form. `words` use sravaṇa.

notes: Complex list; the grammar of 'vedanā ... udarahṛdaya...' is not certain (it could be pain located in these parts followed by the list toda... as its kinds). 'stravaṇa' (st for sr) is read sravaṇa, flow. 'niṣṭīvikā' = spitting (or excess saliva). 'mukta-bandhane iva akṣiṇī' = the eyes as if with loosened bonds. 'basti' here = bladder; hṛdaya = heart (standard). 'yonyāḥ ... sravaṇāni' read as flows of the yoni (vagina); alternative: 'yonyā bhavanti' is correct sandhi of yonyāḥ + bhavanti; 'yonyā' as an instrumental is not adopted.
lines_deva: तत्रासन्नप्रसवायाः क्लमो ग्लानिर्मुक्तबंधने इवाक्षिणी निष्टीविकामूत्रपुरीषबाहुल्यं शिथिलकुक्षिताऽधोगुरुत्वमन्नानभिलाषो वेदनोदरत्हृदयकटीबस्तिवंक्षणेषु तोदभेदशूलस्फुरणस्त्रवणानि च योन्याभवंति
lines_iast: tatrāsannaprasavāyāḥ klamo glānirmuktabaṃdhane ivākṣiṇī niṣṭīvikāmūtrapurīṣabāhulyaṃ śithilakukṣitā'dhogurutvamannānabhilāṣo vedanodarathṛdayakaṭībastivaṃkṣaṇeṣu todabhedaśūlasphuraṇastravaṇāni ca yonyābhavaṃti

hindi: उसके बाद आवियों यानी सम्भवतः प्रसव की पीड़ाओं का प्रकट होना और गर्भोदक यानी गर्भ के जल, उल्बद्रव का बहना।
english: After that, the appearance of the āvīs (probably labour pains) and the flow of the water of the embryo (garbhodaka: amniotic fluid).
notes: āvī = labour pains (probable); garbhodaka = amniotic fluid (probable). No verb in the Sanskrit; none supplied.

hindi: तब उसे, जिसका गर्भ उपस्थित हो, जिसने कौतुक और मंगल किया हो, हाथ में पुंनामफल यानी पुरुष नाम वाला फल, जिसकी पहचान अज्ञात है, लिए हो, भली-भाँति तेल लगी हो, गर्म जल से सींची गई हो, घी सहित यवागू पिलाए।
english: Then one should make her drink gruel (yavāgū) with ghee, her to whom the embryo has come forward, who has performed the kautuka and auspicious rites, with a male-named fruit (puṃnāma-phala, unidentified) in her hand, well anointed with oil and sprinkled with hot water.
notes: 'puṃnāmaphala' = fruit of a masculine name (unidentified); the text does not name the fruit. 'upasthitagarbhā' is literally 'with the embryo arrived/present', i.e. delivery at hand (interpretation not in the text). 'kautuka' = a ritual for protection or auspiciousness; 'svabhyaktā' = well anointed with oil (the oil is not named). 'punnāma' printed with geminate n for puṃ-nāma.
lines_deva: अथैनामुपस्थितगर्भां कृतकौतुकमंगलां पुन्नामफलहस्तां स्वभ्यक्तामुष्णोदकपरिषिक्तां सघृतां यवागूं पाययेत्
lines_iast: athaināmupasthitagarbhāṃ kṛtakautukamaṃgalāṃ punnāmaphalahastāṃ svabhyaktāmuṣṇodakapariṣiktāṃ saghṛtāṃ yavāgūṃ pāyayet

words.gloss: very; red; of a bull; hide; covering

words.gram: pres. part. mid. √śī, f. acc. sg.
pres. part. caus. ā-√śvas, f. nom. pl.

hindi: तब अच्छे लाल बैल के चमड़े के आच्छादन वाली कोमल भूमि की शय्या पर लेटी हुई, उत्तान, जाँघों और पीठ को मोड़े हुए सूतिका को, नए वस्त्र पहने, सन्देह से परे, देखने में प्रिय, प्रौढ़ आयु की, प्रसव में कुशल, निर्भीक, कटे नखों वाली स्त्रियाँ मधुर और सत्य वाणियों से आश्वासन देती हुई घेरकर सेवा करें।
english: Then women with new (unworn) clothes, not to be suspected, pleasant to look at, advanced in age, skilled in delivery, bold, with cut nails, should attend upon the sūtikā (woman in labour) with comforting, pleasant and truthful words, her lying on a soft bed on the ground covered with a very red bull's hide, face upward, with bent thighs and back.

text_flags.why: possible: 'prajanakaśalāḥ' is not a word; 'prajanana-kuśalāḥ' (skilled in delivery) fits; syllables na and ku lost.

notes: 'ābhugnasakthipṛṣṭhām' (with bent thighs and back) is taken as printed; the exact posture is not further described and the text may intend 'bent thighs' with a different word for the back. 'suraktārṣabhacarma' = well-red (or very red) hide of a bull. 'sūtikā' = a woman in childbirth / newly delivered; here in labour by context. 'ahatavāsasaḥ' = with new (unworn) cloth. The women are described by a series of adjectives; 'aśaṅkanīyāḥ' = not to be suspected (trustworthy).
lines_deva: ततः सुरक्तार्षभचर्मप्रच्छदेमृदुनि भूमिशयने शयानामुत्तानामाभुग्नसक्थिपृष्ठामहतवाससोऽशंकनीयाः प्रियदर्शनाः परिणतवयसः प्रजनकशलाः प्रगल्भाः कृत्तनखाः स्त्रियः सूतिकां सूनृताभिर्वाणीभिराश्वासयंत्यः पर्युपासीरन्
lines_iast: tataḥ suraktārṣabhacarmapracchademṛduni bhūmiśayane śayānāmuttānāmābhugnasakthipṛṣṭhāmahatavāsaso'śaṃkanīyāḥ priyadarśanāḥ pariṇatavayasaḥ prajanakaśalāḥ pragalbhāḥ kṛttanakhāḥ striyaḥ sūtikāṃ sūnṛtābhirvāṇībhirāśvāsayaṃtyaḥ paryupāsīran

words.gloss: powder (cūrṇa) of: kuṣṭha (costus, Saussurea costus, standard); elā (small cardamom, Elettaria cardamomum, standard); lāṅgalī (glory lily, Gloriosa superba, standard); vacā (sweet flag, Acorus calamus, standard); cyanya (unclear); citraka (leadwort, Plumbago zeylanica, standard); cirabilva (probably Indian elm, Holoptelea integrifolia, probable)

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, तब इसे कुष्ठ यानी कूठ, एला यानी छोटी इलायची, लाङ्गली यानी कलिहारी, वचा यानी बच, च्यन्य अस्पष्ट शब्द, चित्रक यानी चीता और चिरबिल्व यानी सम्भवतः चिलबिल का चूर्ण बार-बार सूँघने के लिए देना चाहिए।
english: On a conjectural reading: then one should give her, to smell again and again, a powder of kuṣṭha (costus), elā (small cardamom), lāṅgalī (glory lily), vacā (sweet flag), cyanya (unclear), citraka (leadwort) and cirabilva (probably the Indian elm).

text_flags.why: possible: 'cyanya' is not a drug name; cavya (Piper chaba, long-pepper relative) is often paired with citraka and vacā in such lists, and 'cavya' could be misread as 'cyanya'. Not certain, so the word is kept unclear.
possible: 'upāghātum' is not a valid infinitive; 'upāghrātum' (to smell) fits a powder given 'muhurmuhuḥ' (again and again)

notes: Print habit for the whole chunk: anusvāra is written for homorganic nasals (lāṃgalī, jṛṃbhaṇa, maṃdira), and doubled -rtt- (parivarttate) and ṣṭh/ṣṭ and muśala/musala spellings vary; `words` give the standard forms and none of these is flagged again. The compound is a drug list; its fifth member 'cyanya' is unclear in print (kept unsplit, translated as unclear), so the list is read on a conjectural reading. 'upāghātuṃ' is read as upāghrātum (to smell), also conjectural. Verb 'dadyāt' has no stated subject (one/she who attends). Identification tags: kuṣṭha, elā, lāṅgalī, vacā, citraka standard; cirabilva probable. Hindi names: कुष्ठ=कूठ, एला=छोटी इलायची, लाङ्गली=कलिहारी, वचा=बच, चित्रक=चीता, चिरबिल्व=चिलबिल (probable).

words.gloss: birch (bhūrja, Betula utilis, standard); bark (patra); śiśipā (sissoo / Indian rosewood, Dalbergia sissoo, standard); sarja (sāl tree, Shorea robusta, standard)

hindi: वैसे ही भूर्जपत्र यानी भोजपत्र, शिशिपा यानी शीशम, या सर्ज यानी साल के रस, इनमें से किसी एक का धूम यानी धुआँ, बीच-बीच में भी।
english: Likewise, the smoke of any one of birch bark (bhūrjapatra), śiśipā (sissoo) or the sap (rasa) of sarja (sāl), and at intervals.
notes: Elliptical: the verb (dadyāt, 'one should give') is carried from the previous units, so the line is translated without a verb. 'sarja' (end of token 2) and 'rasa' (start of token 3) are read together as sarja-rasa, 'sap of sarja'; the print separates them, and 'rasa' could alternatively be a separate item. The whole is one compound: [bhūrjapatra, śiśipā, sarjarasa]-anyatama-dhūma. 'antarāntarā ca' is read as 'and at intervals' (between the sniffings). Tags: bhūrja, śiśipā, sarja standard; the resin sense of rasa is the usual one but is an interpretation. 'śiśipā' is kept as printed; the usual forms are śiṃśapā or śiśapā (sissoo, Dalbergia sissoo).

words.gloss: regions of: side (pārśva); back (pṛṣṭha); waist/hip (kaṭī); thigh (sakthi)

hindi: उसके पार्श्व, पीठ, कटि और जाँघ के प्रदेशों का गुनगुने तेल से अभ्यंग करके सुखपूर्वक मर्दन करे।
english: Having anointed the regions of her sides, back, waist and thighs with lukewarm oil, one should knead them comfortably.

text_flags.why: possible: 'mṛdgīyāt' is not a form; the optative of mṛd (9th class) is mṛdnīyāt, and sense fits (rubbing after anointing); n/g confusion is common in this print

notes: 'asyā' stands for asyāḥ with the visarga dropped before the voiced m of the next word; this is regular sandhi, not a typo. 'deśa' = region/part. 'tailena' is oil unspecified. The same sandhi applies in units 58, 61, 78 and 82.

hindi: इस प्रकार गर्भ नीचे की ओर पलट जाता है।
english: Thus the fetus (garbha) turns around, downward.
notes: 'avāk' is taken as the adverb 'downward'; the line does not say which part of the fetus leads, and no position is stated. 'evam' refers to the preceding procedure (units 47-49).

hindi: उसका लक्षण।
english: Its sign (lakṣaṇa).
notes: GROUPING: this short unit appears to introduce unit 52, which then states the sign. 'tasya' most likely refers to the turning of the fetus in 50. Copula understood.

hindi: हृदय को छोड़कर वह उदर यानी पेट में प्रवेश करता है और बस्ति यानी सम्भवतः मूत्राशय के सिर को पकड़ लेता है।
english: Having left the heart (hṛdaya), it enters the belly (udara) and takes hold of the head of the bladder (basti, probably).

text_flags.why: possible: ṇh for hṇ (metathesis); avagṛhṇāti (takes hold of) is the standard form

notes: Subject (the fetus, from 50) is not stated here. 'basti' is the bladder in this anatomical context (tag probable); 'śiras' = head/top. 'avagṛṇhāti' is read as avagṛhṇāti (see the flag; a possible metathesis of ṇh). The sign is that the fetus leaves the region of the heart and descends; the text says nothing more.

words.gloss: she is to be made to do

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, वे उसे जल्दी करने को प्रेरित करते हैं, आढ्यः अस्पष्ट शब्द है। यदि वह इस प्रकार नहीं पलटता, तब उससे बार-बार जम्हाई लेना और टहलना कराना चाहिए, और अभी पहले कही गई विधि भी।
english: On a conjectural reading: they urge her on, āḍhyaḥ (unclear). If it does not turn in this way, then she should be made to do yawning and walking about again and again, and the procedure stated just before.

text_flags.why: possible: 'āḍhyaḥ' (nom. sg. 'rich, abounding') makes no sense after 'tvarayanti enām'; possibly a corrupt word for the plural subject of the verb; not resolvable from the print, so it is left unsplit and unclear
possible: stray anusvāra in 'anantaroṃktam'; the sense 'anantara-uktam' (stated just before) fits

notes: 'āḍhyaḥ' is damaged or corrupt, so 'tvarayanti enām' (they hasten her) is translated only on a conjectural reading and without a firm subject. 'kārayitavyā' agrees with an understood 'strī' (the woman, nominative); the three accusatives (yawning, walking about, the procedure) are what she is to be made to do. 'The procedure stated just before' appears to point back to units 47-49. 'parivarttate' (doubled -rtt-) is normalised to parivartate.
lines_deva: त्वरयंत्येनामाढ्यः न चेदेवं परिवर्त्तते ततो मुहुर्मुहुर्जृंभणं चंक्रमणं च कारयितव्याऽनंतरोंक्तं विधिं
lines_iast: tvarayaṃtyenāmāḍhyaḥ na cedevaṃ parivarttate tato muhurmuhurjṛṃbhaṇaṃ caṃkramaṇaṃ ca kārayitavyā'naṃtaroṃktaṃ vidhiṃ

hindi: दूसरे तो कहते हैं कि अनाज से भरी ओखली पर मूसल से प्रहार करना चाहिए।
english: Others, however, say that a mortar filled with grain is to be struck with a pestle.
notes: 'muśala' is a variant spelling of musala (pestle). 'dhānya' is grain, kind not stated. The purpose is not stated in this unit; the next unit rejects this view. The closing 'iti' marks the report of the others' opinion.

hindi: वह तो ठीक नहीं है।
english: That, however, is not right.

text_flags.why: possible: long ū in 'tū' is not needed; 'tat tu' (that, however) is meant

notes: Copula understood. 'tat' refers to the view reported in 54.

hindi: क्योंकि गर्भिणी के लिए कठोर व्यायाम से बचना सदा बताया जाता है।
english: For the avoidance of severe exertion is constantly prescribed for a pregnant woman.
notes: 'garbhiṇyāḥ' (genitive) is rendered 'for a pregnant woman' (genitive of the person concerned). 'vyāyāma' = exertion.

words.gloss: of her in whom all (sarva) dhātus and doṣas are set in motion (pracalita)

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, और विशेषकर प्रसव के समय, जिसके सब धातु और दोष चलायमान हो गए हैं उसके, कोमलता के कारण, त्रार्या अस्पष्ट शब्द है, मुशल्यायाम अस्पष्ट शब्द है, उससे प्रेरित वायु अवसर पाकर प्राणों को हानि पहुँचा सकती है।
english: On a conjectural reading: and especially at the time of delivery, in her whose dhātus and doṣas have all been set in motion, because of delicacy (trāryā, unclear), the wind (vāyu), stirred up by muśalyāyāma (unclear), having found an opening, might injure the vital breaths (prāṇa).

text_flags.why: possible: 'trāryā' is not a word; it may be a corrupt 'nāryāḥ' (of the woman) but this is not certain, so it is kept unclear
possible: 'muśalyāyāma' is not a word; context (units 54-56: pestle, severe exertion) suggests muśala-vyāyāma or muśala-āyāma, 'exertion with a pestle'; not certain
possible: vāyuḥ + antaram should join as 'vāyur antaram'; the r is missing in print

notes: Two damaged words, 'trāryā' and 'muśalyāyāma', are kept unsplit and marked unclear; the sentence is therefore a conjectural reading. 'dhātu-doṣa' in the bahuvrīhi is taken as dvandva 'dhātus and doṣas'. 'antara' = opening/gap (alternative: opportunity). The closing 'iti' gives the reason for the prohibition in 56. 'hiṃsyāt' is a statement of what might happen, not a certain result. The guess muśala-vyāyāma ('exertion with a pestle') comes only from the context of units 54-56 and is kept out of the gloss and translation; see the flag.
lines_deva: विशेषतश्चप्रसवकाले प्रचलितसर्वधातुदोषायाः सौकुमार्यात्त्रार्या मुशल्यायामेनेरितो वायुअंतरं लब्ध्वा प्राणान् हिंस्यादिति
lines_iast: viśeṣataścaprasavakāle pracalitasarvadhātudoṣāyāḥ saukumāryāttrāryā muśalyāyāmenerito vāyuaṃtaraṃ labdhvā prāṇān hiṃsyāditi

hindi: तब कुशल स्त्री, गर्भ के पलट जाने पर उस स्त्री को पलंग पर बिठाकर, बैठी हुई उसके पैरों की ओर से योनि यानी जननमार्ग का अनुलोम दिशा में सुखपूर्वक अभ्यंग करके, दोनों नितम्बों को पैरों से दबाए।
english: Then a skilled woman, having placed her whose fetus has turned on a couch (paryaṅka), and, from the foot-side of her as she sits, having anointed the yoni (vagina) comfortably in the natural direction (anuloma), should press the two buttocks (sphij) with the two feet.
notes: 'pādābhyām' ('with the two feet') does not say whose feet; the natural reading is the attendant's. 'paryaṅka' = couch (alternative: a seated posture). 'anuloma' = in the natural direction (with the grain / downward); the text gives no further detail. The substance anointed is not named. 'niṣaṇṇāyā' = niṣaṇṇāyāḥ with regular visarga loss before y.
lines_deva: अथ परिवृत्तगर्भां पर्यंकमेनामारोप्य कुशला स्त्री पादतोऽस्या निषण्णाया योनिमनुलोममनुसुखमभ्यज्य स्फिजौ पादाभ्यां पीडयेत्
lines_iast: atha parivṛttagarbhāṃ paryaṃkamenāmāropya kuśalā strī pādato'syā niṣaṇṇāyā yonimanulomamanusukhamabhyajya sphijau pādābhyāṃ pīḍayet

hindi: और योनि को बार-बार फैलाए।
english: And she should stretch out the yoni (vagina) again and again.
notes: Subject (the skilled woman of 58) is not stated here. The text does not say how the yoni is stretched.

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, और कहे: हे सौभाग्यवती, धीरे-धीरे प्रवाहण करो यानी जोर लगाओ, तुम्हारे मुख का वर्ण बहुत निर्मल है, तुम पुत्र को जन्म दोगी।
english: On a conjectural reading: and she should say, "O fortunate one, bear down (pravāhaṇa) gently, gently; the colour of your face is very clear; you will bear a son."

text_flags.why: possible: 'suprasanna' + 'ete' makes no sense with 'te mukhavarṇaḥ'; the nominative 'suprasannaḥ te' (your ... very clear) fits
possible: the addressee is 'you', so the 2nd person 'janayiṣyasi' is expected; the printed 3rd person 'janayiṣyati' has no stated subject

notes: Two small corrections (above) are adopted in `words` and marked in the translation. As printed, 'janayiṣyati' would have the face-colour or an unstated 'she' as subject. 'pravāhaṇa' = pushing/bearing down; the speaker (the attendant) addresses the woman in labour. The closing 'iti' ends the quoted speech.
lines_deva: ब्रूयाच्च सुभगे शनैः शनैः प्रवाहयस्व सुप्रसन्नेते मुखवर्णः पुत्रं जनयिष्यतीति
lines_iast: brūyācca subhage śanaiḥ śanaiḥ pravāhayasva suprasannete mukhavarṇaḥ putraṃ janayiṣyatīti

hindi: दूसरी तो इसके बाएँ कान में यह मन्त्र जपे। पृथ्वी, जल, आकाश, तेज यानी अग्नि, वायु, विष्णु, प्रजापति।
english: Another (woman), however, should mutter this mantra in her left ear. Earth, water, sky (viyat), fire (tejas), wind, Viṣṇu, Prajāpati.
notes: [02.03.61] 'anyā' is feminine, so another woman is meant; the noun is not stated. The mantra follows in 62 onward. [02.03.62] GROUPING: this list of names (the mantra) has no verb; it appears to continue in unit 63, whose verbs (pātu, dadhātu) probably have these as subjects. The verbs in 63 are singular although seven names are listed.

words.gram: ppp. a-vi-√kliś, m. acc. sg. or adv.

hindi: गर्भ सहित तुम्हारी सदा रक्षा करे, या शल्य से मुक्ति भी प्रदान करे। हे सुन्दर मुख वाली, अपीड़ित तुम अपीड़ित को जन्म दो।
english: May (it) always protect you, together with the fetus, or also grant freedom from the dart (śalya). Give birth, you who are unharmed, to the unharmed (one), O fair-faced one.
notes: [02.03.63] GROUPING: appears to continue 62. Subject is not stated in this unit; the verbs are singular, probably agreeing with the list in 62 taken together. 'śalya' = dart (also a foreign body or a piercing pain); its precise sense here is not certain, so it is not interpreted. 'vaiśalya' = state without the dart. The sense of 'vā ... api' ('or ... also') is loose. [02.03.64] GROUPING: appears to continue in 65, where 'putram' (son) is the object, so the first 'avikliṣṭam' most likely agrees with it; it could instead be the adverb 'without distress'. The printed letter ḻ (in avikḻiṣṭa) is normalised to l, a print habit recorded once for this book.
lines_deva: सगर्भां त्वां सदापातु वैशल्यं वा दधात्वपि
lines_iast: sagarbhāṃ tvāṃ sadāpātu vaiśalyaṃ vā dadhātvapi

hindi: कार्तिकेय की कान्ति वाले, कार्तिकेय से रक्षित पुत्र को।
english: A son having the splendour of Kārtikeya, protected by Kārtikeya.
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'prasūṣva' (give birth) is carried from 64, so no verb is supplied. Kārtikeya is the name of a god, as printed. The closing 'iti' ends the mantra.

hindi: तथा।
english: Likewise.
notes: Connecting word before a second mantra (67 onward).

words.gloss: Citrabhānu (bright-rayed; an epithet of fire or sun)
in the house, in the abode

hindi: यहाँ अमृत और सोम और चित्रभानु, हे भामिनी। और उच्चैःश्रवा घोड़ा तुम्हारे घर में निवास करें।
english: Here: nectar (amṛta), and Soma, and Citrabhānu, O lady. And Uccaiḥśravas, the horse: may (they) dwell in your house.
notes: [02.03.67] GROUPING: no verb here; the plural verb 'nivasantu' in 68 appears to complete this line. 'citrabhānu' is an epithet (of fire or the sun); which is meant is not stated, so only the epithet is given. [02.03.68] GROUPING: appears to continue 67; the plural verb probably has amṛta, Soma, Citrabhānu and Uccaiḥśravas as subjects. 'te' is taken as 'your' (alternatively 'to you'). 'mandira' is house/dwelling.

hindi: जलों से निकाला गया यह अमृत निश्चय ही, हे स्त्री, तुम्हारे इस गर्भ को शीघ्र छोड़ दे।
english: This nectar (amṛta), indeed drawn up from the waters: may it quickly release this fetus of yours, O woman.
notes: 'stri' is the regular vocative of strī. 'laghu' is taken as the adverb 'quickly' (alternative: lightly, easily).
lines_deva: इदममृतमपां समुद्धृतं वै तव लघु गर्भमिमं प्रमुंचतु स्त्रि
lines_iast: idamamṛtamapāṃ samuddhṛtaṃ vai tava laghu garbhamimaṃ pramuṃcatu stri

hindi: अनुमानित पाठ पर, इसलिए अग्नि, वायु, सूर्य और इन्द्र, लवण जल धारण करने वालों के साथ, तुम्हें शान्ति दें।
english: On a conjectural reading: therefore may fire (anala), wind (pavana), sun (arka) and Indra (Vāsava), together with the bearers of salt water, grant you peace (śānti).

text_flags.why: possible: 'analpavana' (a-l-p-a-v) is not a word; anala-pavana (fire, wind) fits the list with arka and Vāsava, and a short 'a' looks dropped after 'l' (analpavana for analapavana)

notes: The list reading depends on the correction above. 'te' is taken as the enclitic 'to you' (alternative: 'they'). 'lavaṇāmbudhara' is literally 'bearer(s) of salt water'; whether oceans or clouds is not clear, so it is left literal. 'arka' = sun here (arka is also a plant name). 'tat' = therefore (alternative: that).

hindi: वैसे ही दूसरी समझाए।
english: Likewise another (woman) should instruct (her).
notes: 'parā' is feminine, so a woman is meant. The object (the woman in labour) is not stated; the instruction appears to follow in 72-76.

hindi: वेदना के न आने पर प्रवाहण मत करो।
english: When the pain (vedanā) has not come, do not bear down.

text_flags.why: possible: 'praivāhiṭṭāḥ' is not a form; mā + the aorist 'pravāhiṣṭhāḥ' (do not bear down) fits, and unit 75 has the same verb as 'prabāhiṣṭāḥ'

notes: The aorist form of pra-√vah (instead of the causative used in 60, pravāhayasva) is as printed in both 72 and 75; the grammar is not fully certain, but the sense is clear from 73. vedanā 'pain' here is probably the pain of labour (contractions), a reading from context (probable).

words.gloss: bearing down at the wrong time
of the urges (vega) of feces, urine and the rest
because of causing: breathlessness (śvāsa, standard); cough (kāsa, standard); wasting (śoṣa, probable); hunchedness (kubjatā); and so on

hindi: असमय प्रवाहण मल, मूत्र आदि के वेगों को जबरन निकालने के समान है, निरर्थक है और गर्भ के लिए अहितकर है, क्योंकि वह श्वास यानी साँस फूलना, कास यानी खाँसी, शोष यानी सूखकर घटते जाना, कुब्जता यानी कूबड़ापन आदि करता है।
english: For bearing down at the wrong time (akāla-pravāhaṇa) is like forcing out the urges (vega) of feces, urine and the rest; it is useless and unwholesome for the fetus, because it causes breathlessness (śvāsa), cough (kāsa), wasting (śoṣa), hunchedness (kubjatā) and so on.
notes: Copula understood. 'garbhasya' is taken with 'ahitam' (unwholesome for the fetus); it could also go with the list of harms. The harms are stated by the text as consequences of untimely bearing down. 'śoṣa' = wasting (in older usage sometimes consumption); kept as 'wasting'. 'anarthakaram' is rendered 'useless'; an alternative is 'causing harm/trouble' (anartha = harm).

hindi: वैसे ही वेदना में प्रवाहण न करना उन्हीं के रोकने के समान है, हानि के लिए होता है।
english: Likewise, not bearing down when there is pain (vedanā), like the holding back of those very (urges), is for injury.
notes: 'teṣām' refers back to the urges (vega) in 73. Copula understood; 'upaghātāya' (dative of purpose) is rendered 'leads to injury'. The text does not say what injury.

hindi: तब जैसा कहा गया है वैसा करो, धीरे-धीरे, और पहले प्रवाहण करो।
english: Then do as stated, gently, gently, and at first bear down.

text_flags.why: possible: b/v confusion and lost -h-; same verb as in unit 72 (pravāhiṣṭhāḥ)

notes: GROUPING: 75 and 76 appear to form one sentence about the stages of bearing down. 'pūrvam' = first/at first.
lines_deva: ततो यथोक्तं कुरुष्व शनैः शनैश्च पूर्वं प्रबाहिष्टाः
lines_iast: tato yathoktaṃ kuruṣva śanaiḥ śanaiśca pūrvaṃ prabāhiṣṭāḥ

words.gloss: on arrival at the mouth of the yoni

hindi: गर्भ के निकलने पर जोर से, योनि के मुख तक पहुँचने पर और अधिक जोर से, प्रसव तक।
english: Strongly at the exit of the fetus; more strongly on arrival at the mouth of the yoni, until delivery.
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'pravāhiṣṭhāḥ' (bear down) is carried from 75, so none is supplied. 'garbhasya' probably governs both 'nirgame' and 'pratipattau'. The closing 'iti' ends the instruction.

words.gram: pres. part. mid. pra-√vah, f. gen. sg.

hindi: उस प्रवाहण करती हुई स्त्री के लिए वे यह शब्द करें: जन्म दे दिया, जन्म दे दिया, धन्य, धन्य पुत्र को!
english: For that woman who is bearing down, they should raise a cry: "She has given birth, she has given birth, to a blessed, blessed son!"
notes: The genitives 'tasyāḥ ... striyāḥ' are taken as 'for/over that woman'; the exact relation is loose. The subject of 'kuryuḥ' (they) is not stated. 'prajātā' is used actively ('has given birth'). 'dhanya' = blessed (alternatively fortunate).
lines_deva: तस्यास्तु प्रवाहमानायाः स्त्रियाः शब्दं कुर्युः प्रजाता प्रजाता धन्यंधन्यं पुत्रमिति
lines_iast: tasyāstu pravāhamānāyāḥ striyāḥ śabdaṃ kuryuḥ prajātā prajātā dhanyaṃdhanyaṃ putramiti

hindi: इस प्रकार उसके प्राण हर्ष से पुष्ट होते हैं।
english: Thus her vital breaths (prāṇa) are nourished by joy.
notes: 'āpyāyyante' = are nourished/refreshed/swollen; rendered 'nourished'. The cry of 77 appears to be the cause of the joy.

words.gloss: in retention (obstruction) of the fetus; garbha-saṅga, probably obstructed labour (probable)
with the sloughed skin of a black snake
with piṇḍītaka (probably emetic nut, Randia dumetorum, probable)

hindi: गर्भसंग यानी गर्भ के रुकने में, योनि यानी जननमार्ग को काले साँप की केंचुली से या पिण्डीतक यानी सम्भवतः मैनफल से धूपित करे।
english: In garbha-saṅga (retention of the fetus; probably obstructed labour), one should fumigate the yoni (vagina) with the sloughed skin of a black snake, or with piṇḍītaka (probably the emetic nut).
notes: 'saṅga' = sticking/obstruction; the modern equivalent 'obstructed labour' is a probable reading, not stated. 'kṛṣṇasarpa' is literally 'black snake'; the species is not stated. 'nirmokena' is printed with n for ṇ (orthographic). piṇḍītaka is commonly equated with madana (Randia dumetorum) but the identity is not certain.
lines_deva: गर्भसंगे तुयोनिं धूपयेत् कृष्णसर्पनिर्मोकेन पिंडीतकेन वा
lines_iast: garbhasaṃge tuyoniṃ dhūpayet kṛṣṇasarpanirmokena piṃḍītakena vā

hindi: और हिरण्यपुष्पी की जड़, जिसकी पहचान अज्ञात है, हाथ और पैर में बाँधे।
english: And one should tie the root of hiraṇyapuṣpī (unidentified) on the hand and foot.
notes: 'hiraṇyapuṣpī' (literally 'golden-flowered') is not identified here: sources differ and no safe identification is given. 'hastapāde' is a singular collective 'hand and foot'; the text does not say whose or whether both sides. The 'if' condition of 79 (garbha-saṅga) appears to carry on into 80 and 81; it is not repeated here.

hindi: और सुवर्चला, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, या विशल्या, जो सम्भवतः लाङ्गली यानी कलिहारी है, धारण करे।
english: And one should hold suvarcalā (identity disputed) or viśalyā (probably the same as lāṅgalī).
notes: GROUPING: 80 and 81 appear to continue one another (things to tie or hold). suvarcalā is disputed (candidates include Cleome gynandra and others); viśalyā is a recognised synonym of lāṅgalī (Gloriosa superba) in the drug lists, tagged probable.

hindi: अब यदि प्रसव कर चुकी स्त्री का अपरा यानी जेर नहीं गिरता, तब दाहिने हाथ से नाभि के ऊपर से जोर से दबाकर और पीछे की ओर से पकड़कर हिलाए।
english: Now, if the placenta (aparā) of one who has delivered does not fall out, then, pressing firmly with the right hand from above the navel and gripping from behind, one should shake.

text_flags.why: possible: ṣṭh for ṣṭ in upariṣṭāt (from above); the aspirate looks like a misprint

notes: 'prasūtāyā na' is regular sandhi for prasūtāyāḥ na. The object of 'upasaṅgṛhya' and 'vidhūnuyāt' is not stated (not even the abdomen), so none is supplied; 'upariṣṭhāt' is printed with ṣṭh (read as upariṣṭāt; see the flag). 'aparā' = placenta/afterbirth (standard).
lines_deva: अथ प्रसूतायान चेदपरा पतति ततो दक्षिणेन पाणिना नाभेरुपरिष्ठाद्बलवदुपपीड्यपृष्ठत उपसंगृह्य विधूनुयात्
lines_iast: atha prasūtāyāna cedaparā patati tato dakṣiṇena pāṇinā nābherupariṣṭhādbalavadupapīḍyapṛṣṭhata upasaṃgṛhya vidhūnuyāt

hindi: या एड़ी से श्रोणि यानी कूल्हे पर प्रहार करे।
english: Or one should strike the hip (śroṇi) with the heel.

text_flags.why: possible: instrumental 'pāṣṇyā' (with the heel) is expected; the anusvāra looks like a stray mark (a locative would be 'pāṣṇyām', 'on the heel')

notes: 'śroṇi' = hip/pelvic region (alternative: buttock). The text does not say whose heel. Elliptical: the 'if the placenta does not fall' condition of 82 appears to carry on here; it is not repeated.

hindi: या दोनों नितम्बों को पकड़कर खूब दबाए।
english: Or, having gripped the two buttocks (sphij), one should press them thoroughly.
notes: 'supīḍitam pīḍayet' is a cognate expression, 'press so that it is well pressed'. Elliptical: the 'if the placenta does not fall' condition of 82 appears to carry on here; it is not repeated.

hindi: वेणी से, या बालों से लिपटी अँगुली से, कण्ठ और तालु को स्पर्श करे।
english: With a braid, or with a finger wound round with hair, one should touch the throat (kaṇṭha) and palate (tālu).
notes: 'keśaveṣṭitayā' is taken with 'aṅgulyā' (the finger wound with hair); it could also go with 'veṇyā'. The text states no effect of the touch. Elliptical: the 'if the placenta does not fall' condition of 82 appears to carry on here; it is not repeated.

words.gloss: with birch bark (bhūrjapatra); kāca-maṇi (literally 'glass-gem', sense doubtful); snake slough
with bhūrja (birch) and guggulu (Indian bdellium, Commiphora wightii, standard)

hindi: और भूर्जपत्र यानी भोजपत्र, काचमणि जिसका अर्थ यहाँ संदिग्ध है, और साँप की केंचुली से योनि यानी जननमार्ग को धूपित करे, या भूर्ज और गुग्गुल से।
english: And one should fumigate the yoni (vagina) with birch bark (bhūrjapatra), kāca-maṇi (literally 'glass-gem'; sense doubtful) and snake slough, or with bhūrja and guggulu (Indian bdellium).
notes: 'kāca-maṇi' is taken literally (glass + gem/bead); fumigating with glass is odd, so the word may be corrupt (for example a plant name); not resolved and not interpreted. The print joins 'dhūpayet' to 'bhūrja' (no space). 'nirmoka' = slough. Elliptical: the 'if the placenta does not fall' condition of 82 appears to carry on here; it is not repeated.

words.gloss: cooked with the root of śāli (a rice variety, Oryza sativa)
with bitter bottle gourd (kaṭukālābu, Lagenaria siceraria, probable); jālinī (a Luffa, disputed); nimba (neem, Azadirachta indica, standard); snake slough

hindi: या शालि यानी धान की एक किस्म की जड़ के साथ पकाए घी से योनि का अभ्यंग करके सम्भवतः कड़वी लौकी, जालिनी यानी सम्भवतः तोरई जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, निम्ब यानी नीम और साँप की केंचुली से धूपन करे।
english: Or, having anointed the yoni (vagina) with ghee cooked with the root of śāli (a variety of rice), one should fumigate with probably bitter bottle gourd (kaṭukālābu), jālinī (a Luffa; disputed), nimba (neem) and snake slough.

text_flags.why: possible: the a of abhyajya is lost in print
possible: ḍ for ṭ in 'kaduka'; 'alāmbu' (a variant of alābu) is normalised to alābu in `words`

notes: 'kaṭukālābu' is read as one drug, 'bitter bottle gourd'; the alternative is two drugs, kaṭukā (probably Picrorhiza kurroa) and alābu. 'śāli' is a rice variety; 'śālimūla' could in principle be a shortened name of another plant, so only the literal sense is given. 'siddha' = cooked. 'jālinī' is disputed (Luffa species are the usual guess). Elliptical: the 'if the placenta does not fall' condition of 82 appears to carry on through 83-92.

words.gloss: mixed with kaṭu oil (pungent oil, probably mustard oil, probable)

hindi: या जिसका अभ्यंग न हुआ हो उसे, कटुतैल यानी सम्भवतः सरसों के तेल से मिले हुए, कल्क बनाए हुए, या तेल से लिपे हुए से लेप करे।
english: Or, for one not anointed, one should smear with (ones) mixed with kaṭu oil (probably mustard oil), made into a paste (kalka), or smeared with oil.
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 87. The nouns are not stated: 'anabhyaktām' (feminine, probably the yoni or the woman) and the three instrumentals (probably the fumigants of 87, but not stated) are left as in the Sanskrit. The structure of the two 'vā' is uncertain. 'kaṭu-taila' (pungent oil) is probably mustard oil, a modern reading.

words.gloss: with a paste (kalka) of jaggery (guḍa) and dry ginger (nāgara, Zingiber officinale, standard)

hindi: या गुड़ और नागर यानी सोंठ के कल्क से।
english: Or with a paste (kalka) of jaggery (guḍa) and dry ginger (nāgara).
notes: Elliptical: the verb 'ālimpet' (should smear) is carried from 88, so none is supplied. The next unit says that this very paste may be eaten.

hindi: या उसी को खाए।
english: Or one should eat that very (paste).
notes: 'tat' most probably refers to the guḍa-nāgara paste of 89; the noun is not stated. The subject is not stated (probably the woman).

words.gloss: with a paste (kalka) of lāṅgalī root
milk (sap) of mahāvṛkṣa (disputed, probably a spurge such as snuhī)

hindi: या लाङ्गली यानी कलिहारी की जड़ के कल्क से हाथ और पेट पर लेप करे। या महावृक्ष, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, सम्भवतः थूहर, का दूध सिर पर डाले।
english: Or with a paste (kalka) of lāṅgalī (glory lily) root one should smear the hand and the belly (udara). Or one should pour the milk (kṣīra) of mahāvṛkṣa (disputed; probably snuhī, a spurge) over the head.

text_flags.why: possible: short u in 'mula'; 'mūla' (root) is the expected word

notes: [02.03.91] 'pāṇim' is singular ('hand'); the text does not say whether one or both hands. lāṅgalī: see unit 47. Appears to continue the placenta remedies of 82 onward. [02.03.92] 'mahāvṛkṣa' (literally 'great tree') is a drug name whose identity varies by source; tagged disputed. 'kṣīra' of a plant = milky sap (latex). Appears to continue the placenta remedies of 82 onward.

words.gloss: vyoṣa (the three pungents: dry ginger, long pepper, black pepper; standard); sharp; hot
horse gram (kulattha, Macrotyloma uniflorum; standard); juice
madhuka (licorice, Glycyrrhiza glabra; probable); pippalī (long pepper; standard); cooking together

hindi: कुष्ठ यानी कूठ और अस्पष्ट शब्द ताली को कल्क के साथ पिलाना चाहिए: बिल्व यानी बेल, बिल्वज, यूष, मैरेय, आसव, सुरा और सुरामण्ड में से किसी एक के साथ; या व्योष यानी सोंठ, पीपर और काली मिर्च से तीखे और गरम खट्टे के साथ; या कुलथी के रस के साथ; या मधुक यानी सम्भवतः मुलेठी और पिप्पली यानी पीपर के संपाक के साथ।
english: Kuṣṭha (costus) and tālī (unclear), with paste (kalka), should be given to drink with any one of bilva (bael), bilvaja (unclear), soup (yūṣa), maireya, āsava, surā and surā-maṇḍa; or with a sour (one) that is sharp and hot with vyoṣa (the three pungents); or with horse-gram (kulattha) juice; or with a cooking together of madhuka (probably licorice) and pippalī (long pepper).

text_flags.why: possible: dental n printed for ṇ; unit 104 prints surāmaṇḍena

notes: Object of pāyayet is not stated. 'tālī' is unclear: possibly a truncated tālīsa (Abies webbiana, disputed) but the printed word is kept and not enriched. 'bilvabilvajayūṣa' could also be read as 'bilva' + 'bilvaja-yūṣa'; bilvaja is unclear; unit 95 treats 'bilvabilvajayūṣādi' as the head of a list of āplavana (dips). 'vyoṣa-tīkṣṇoṣṇena amlena' read as one sour (one) made sharp and hot with vyoṣa. madhuka = licorice is probable (Madhuca is another possibility). Sentence is elliptical and follows earlier units on childbirth. REVIEW: alternative division of the printed 'kuṣṭhatālī sakalkaṃ' = kuṣṭha-tālīsa-kalkam (a paste of kuṣṭha and tālīsa, with the space misplaced); this would supply the missing object of pāyayet, as in units 94, 96, 98. Not adopted; owner to decide.
lines_deva: कुष्ठताली सकल्कं बिल्वबिल्वजयूषमैरेयासवसुरामन्दान्यतमेन व्योषतीक्ष्णोष्णेन वाऽम्लेन कुलत्थरसेन मधुकपिप्पलीसंपाकेन वा पाययेत्
lines_iast: kuṣṭhatālī sakalkaṃ bilvabilvajayūṣamaireyāsavasurāmandānyatamena vyoṣatīkṣṇoṣṇena vā'mlena kulattharasena madhukapippalīsaṃpākena vā pāyayet

hindi: या पिप्पली यानी पीपर, एला यानी सम्भवतः इलायची, कोल यानी सम्भवतः बेर का फल, विड नामक द्रव्य, चव्य यानी सम्भवतः चव, चित्रक यानी चीता और उपकुञ्चिका यानी सम्भवतः कलौंजी जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, का कल्क।
english: Or a paste (kalka) of pippalī (long pepper), elā (probably cardamom), kola (probably jujube fruit), viḍa (drug name), cavya (probably Piper chaba), citraka (leadwort) and upakuñcikā (probably nigella; identity disputed).
notes: Elliptical: 'vā' continues the list of options from 93 and the verb 'should be given to drink' is carried from there, none supplied. Identifications: kola jujube and cavya probable; upakuñcikā nigella disputed (some read upakuñcikā as black cumin or fennel-like seed); viḍa is a drug name only (glossary).

words.gloss: of those beginning with bilva, bilvaja and yūṣa

hindi: गधे या बैल के जीवित रहते उसका दाहिना कान निकालकर, बिल्व, बिल्वज और यूष आदि आप्लवनों में से किसी एक में डालकर, मुहूर्त भर रहने पर निकालकर, उस आप्लवन को पिलाना चाहिए।
english: Having taken out the right ear of a living donkey or bull, and having put it into any one of the dips (āplavana) beginning with bilva, bilvaja and yūṣa, and having taken it out after it has stayed a muhūrta, one should give that dip to drink.
notes: 'muhūrtasthitam' (accusative, agreeing with karṇam) = the ear that has stayed for a muhūrta (a short period, about 48 minutes in standard reckoning; not stated in the text). 'jīvataḥ' could agree with the animal; read as 'of the living (one)'. 'tadāplavanam' read tad + āplavanam. 'āplavana' = dip/immersion liquid; sense of the list is as in 93.
lines_deva: खरस्य वृषभस्य वा जीवतो दक्षिणं कर्णमुद्धृत्य बिल्वबिल्वजयूषादीनामाप्लवनानामन्यतमे प्रक्षिप्य मुहूर्तस्थितमुद्धृत्य तदाप्लवनं पाययेत्
lines_iast: kharasya vṛṣabhasya vā jīvato dakṣiṇaṃ karṇamuddhṛtya bilvabilvajayūṣādīnāmāplavanānāmanyatame prakṣipya muhūrtasthitamuddhṛtya tadāplavanaṃ pāyayet

hindi: या कुष्ठ यानी कूठ और एला यानी सम्भवतः इलायची का कल्क सुरा के साथ।
english: Or a paste (kalka) of kuṣṭha (costus) and elā (probably cardamom) with surā (grain liquor).
notes: Elliptical: verb ('should be given to drink') carried from 93 and none supplied.

words.gloss: arka (calotrope, Calotropis; probable); ala (unclear); arka; decoction

hindi: या अर्क यानी आक, अस्पष्ट शब्द अला और अर्क का काढ़ा, सुरा में मिलाया हुआ।
english: Or a decoction of arka (calotrope), ala (unclear) and arka, mixed with surā.

text_flags.why: possible: printed 'arkālerka' has e (arka-ale-arka); 'alarka' (white-flowered calotrope, disputed) would read arka-alarka-kaṣāyam; unclear, printed form not restored

notes: Split of 'arkālerka' is doubtful: arka + ale/ala + arka, or arka + alarka (alarka is a name for a kind of arka, usually called white calotrope; disputed). Kept unenriched and the middle word is marked unclear. kaṣāya here is the preparation, decoction. 'suronmiśram' = surā + unmiśram, by regular ā + u > o sandhi, no shortening; the verb is carried from 93.

words.gloss: kuṣṭha (costus); lāṅgalī (gloriosa lily, Gloriosa superba; probable); root; paste
madya (an intoxicating drink); urine; with either one

hindi: या कुष्ठ और लाङ्गली यानी सम्भवतः कलिहारी की जड़ का कल्क, मद्य या मूत्र में से किसी एक के साथ।
english: Or a paste (kalka) of kuṣṭha (costus) and the root of lāṅgalī (probably gloriosa lily), with either madya (an intoxicating drink) or urine.

text_flags.why: possible: short u for ū in mūla and 'vā' joined without a space

notes: The urine is not specified (of which animal); none supplied. 'mūla' may belong to lāṅgalī only or to both (kuṣṭha root): read 'root of lāṅgalī'. Verb carried from 93. anyatareṇa = with either of two.

words.gloss: vatsaka (kutaja seed, Holarrhena; probable); beginning with; powder

hindi: या वत्सक आदि का चूर्ण मद्य के साथ।
english: Or the powder of the group beginning with vatsaka, with madya (an intoxicating drink).
notes: 'vatsakādi' = the group beginning with vatsaka (probably the kuṭaja seed, Holarrhena antidysenterica; the group's members are not listed here). Verb carried from 93.

hindi: और शतपुष्पा यानी सम्भवतः सौंफ या सोआ, कुष्ठ, मदन यानी सम्भवतः मैनफल और हींग के साथ पकाए हुए तेल का पिचु यानी रुई का फाहा पकड़वाना चाहिए।
english: And a picu (cotton wad) of oil cooked with śatapuṣpā (probably dill), kuṣṭha, madana (probably emetic nut) and hiṅgu (asafoetida) should be made to be held.

text_flags.why: possible: 'ca' joined without a space

notes: Printed 'siddhasyaca' is siddhasya + ca; the 'ca' is translated 'and' (it links this unit to the preceding options). 'picu' = a pledget or wad of cotton; 'soaked in' is not in the text, so the translation says 'a picu of oil cooked with ...'; in Hindi picu is glossed as cotton wad. Hindi names dill/fennel hedged because the identity is probable only. Place of use (probably the vagina) not stated. Dill identity for śatapuṣpā is probable (fennel also proposed).

words.gloss: at the time of anuvāsana (oil enema)

hindi: फिर इसे अनुवासन यानी तेल की बस्ति के समय अनुवासन देना चाहिए।
english: And then, at the time of anuvāsana (oil enema), one should give her an anuvāsana.
notes: 'anuvāsana' = oil enema (standard); the denominative verb anuvāsayet is rendered 'should give an anuvāsana'. 'enām' (her) refers to the woman of the earlier units; not stated here.

words.gloss: dips (āplavana) beginning with bilva, bilvaja and yūṣa (soup)

hindi: और बिल्व, बिल्वज और यूष आदि आप्लवनों से।
english: And with the dips (āplavana) beginning with bilva, bilvaja and yūṣa (soup).
notes: GROUPING: appears to continue 103 (the instrumental 'with the dips ... ' goes with the verb āsthāpayet there) or the anuvāsana of 101; the printed unit has no verb. None supplied. Bilvaja is unclear (see 93).

words.gloss: phala (fruit; here probably madana fruit, not firm)
ikṣvāku (bitter bottle gourd, Lagenaria siceraria; probable)

hindi: फल, जीमूतक यानी सम्भवतः देवदाली, इक्ष्वाकु यानी सम्भवतः कड़वी लौकी, धामार्गव यानी पहचान विवादित द्रव्य, कुटज यानी कुड़ा, अस्पष्ट शब्द आकै, कृतवेधन यानी सम्भवतः तोरई और हस्तिपर्णी, जिसकी पहचान अज्ञात है, से युक्त किए हुए से आस्थापन देना चाहिए।
english: One should give an āsthāpana (decoction enema) with (ones) furnished with phala, jīmūtaka (probably a Luffa gourd), ikṣvāku (probably bitter bottle gourd), dhāmārgava (identity disputed), kuṭaja, ākai (unclear), kṛtavedhana (probably ridge gourd) and hastiparṇī (unidentified).

text_flags.why: possible: 'kuṭajākaikṛtavedhana' is unclear; 'ākai' may be a damaged 'arka' ('kuṭaja-arka-kṛtavedhana') but this is only a guess and the printed form is kept unsplit as 'ākai' (unclear)

notes: Unrestorable: 'ākai'. 'phala' alone is not firmly identified (in this tradition often madana fruit, but the text does not say). 'those (liquids)' that are furnished are not stated; '(ones)' shows this. Identifications of the gourds follow common lists; scholars differ. The unit shape suggests it continues from 102.

words.gloss: śālmalī (silk-cotton tree, Bombax ceiba; standard); stalks

hindi: सिद्धार्थक यानी सफेद सरसों, कुष्ठ, लाङ्गली और महावृक्ष, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, के दूध से मिले हुए के साथ, या सुरामण्ड के साथ, शाल्मली के डण्ठल या अस्पष्ट शब्द स्त्रिञ्चानि को कूटकर पञ्चमूल के काढ़े में मसलना चाहिए।
english: With (one) mixed with siddhārthaka (probably white mustard), kuṣṭha, lāṅgalī and the milk (kṣīra) of mahāvṛkṣa (identity disputed), or with surā-maṇḍa; the stalks of śālmalī (silk-cotton tree) or striñcāni (unclear) having been pounded, one should crush (them) in a decoction of the five roots (pañcamūla).

text_flags.why: possible: 'striñcāni' is not a known word and the print may be damaged; kept unsplit and marked unclear

notes: The sentence is elliptical and its syntax is uncertain: the first instrumental phrase presumably qualifies the liquid used, but the noun is not stated. 'vā' after śālmalīvṛntāni is read 'or', joining striñcāni to the stalks; this is a guess. The Hindi and English both mark striñcāni unclear. pañcamūla may be the greater or the lesser five roots (not stated). mahāvṛkṣa disputed (sometimes a Euphorbia). Probably continues the enema recipes of 103.
lines_deva: सिद्धार्थककुष्ठलाङ्गलीमहावृक्षक्षीरमिश्रेण वा सुरामण्डेन शाल्मलीवृन्तानि वा स्त्रिञ्चान्यापोथ्यपञ्चमूलकषाये विमर्दयेत्
lines_iast: siddhārthakakuṣṭhalāṅgalīmahāvṛkṣakṣīramiśreṇa vā surāmaṇḍena śālmalīvṛntāni vā striñcānyāpothyapañcamūlakaṣāye vimardayet

words.gloss: joined with phala and the rest
cooked with the substances of the āsthāpana as stated

hindi: और उस छाने हुए, स्नेह वाले, फल आदि से युक्त, यथोक्त आस्थापन द्रव्यों से पकाए हुए कटु तेल यानी सम्भवतः सरसों के तेल से उत्तरबस्ति यानी मूत्रमार्ग या गर्भाशय में दी जाने वाली बस्ति देनी चाहिए।
english: And with that, strained, oily, joined with phala and the rest, with pungent oil (kaṭutaila; probably mustard oil) cooked with the substances of the āsthāpana as stated, one should give an uttarabasti (urethral or uterine injection).
notes: The adjectives (tena pūtena snehavatā phalādiyuktena ...) may all qualify kaṭutaila or may describe a separate liquid; the grammar allows both, so the literal order is kept. kaṭutaila is probably mustard oil (probable), literally 'pungent oil'. uttarabasti is the standard term for an injection through the urethra or the female passage; the text does not say which here.
lines_deva: तेन च पूतेन स्नेहवता फलादियुक्तेन यथोक्तास्थापनद्रव्यसिद्धेन कटुतैलेनोत्तरबस्तिं दद्यात्
lines_iast: tena ca pūtena snehavatā phalādiyuktena yathoktāsthāpanadravyasiddhena kaṭutailenottarabastiṃ dadyāt

hindi: या शिग्रु यानी सहजन, सुमुख यानी सम्भवतः एक तुलसी, मरिच यानी काली मिर्च, अजाजी यानी सम्भवतः जीरा और चित्रक यानी चीता के कल्क, दूध और गोमूत्र से पकाए हुए कटु तेल यानी सम्भवतः सरसों के तेल से अनुवासन देना चाहिए।
english: Or one should give an anuvāsana (oil enema) with pungent oil (kaṭutaila; probably mustard oil) cooked with the paste of śigru (drumstick), sumukha (probably a basil), marica (black pepper), ajājī (probably cumin) and citraka, with milk and with cow's urine.
notes: Taken as: the paste is of the first five, then milk and cow's urine. sumukha is a disputed plant name in some lists (a basil is the usual guess, probable). 'ā' in kaṭutailenā'nuvāsayet is the print's habit for a + a (kaṭutailena + anuvāsayet).

words.gloss: umā (flax, Linum usitatissimum; probable); śālmalī; picchā (probably silk-cotton gum)

hindi: या घी सहित उमा यानी सम्भवतः अलसी और शाल्मली की पिच्छा से योनि को भरकर हिलाना चाहिए। या स्नेहयुक्त, कटे नाखून वाले हाथ से माला के अनुसार हटाना चाहिए। यहाँ माला का अर्थ अस्पष्ट है।
english: Or, having filled the yoni (female genital passage) with picchā of umā (probably flax) and śālmalī together with ghee, one should shake. Or with an oiled hand with the nails cut, one should remove, following the mālā (garland or row; sense unclear).
notes: [02.03.107] picchā is probably the gum or mucilage of śālmalī (probable); the text only says picchā. umā: flax is the usual identification (probable), but umā is also a name of turmeric or other plants. Object of vidhunuyāt not stated. [02.03.108] mālā is kept as 'garland, row' with its sense unclear in this context (not enriched). The object of apaharet is not stated, and none is supplied. snigdha is rendered 'oiled' (could also be 'unctuous').
lines_deva: उमाशाल्मलीपिच्छया वा सघृतया योनिं पूरयित्वा विधुनुयात्
lines_iast: umāśālmalīpicchayā vā saghṛtayā yoniṃ pūrayitvā vidhunuyāt

words.gloss: in one who has given birth
called makkala (makkalla, a post-partum pain; standard spelling makkalla)

hindi: यदि जन्म दे चुकी में बस्ति यानी मूत्राशय और अस्पष्ट शब्द मुद्धोदर में मक्कल नाम की पीड़ा हो।
english: If, in one who has given birth, there is a pain called makkala in the basti (bladder) and muddhodareṣu (unclear).

text_flags.why: possible: 'muddhodareṣu' is unclear (perhaps mūrdha-udareṣu or similar); kept unsplit
possible: the usual spelling is makkalla (double l)

notes: GROUPING: the unit is a protasis (if-clause); the apodosis is in 110 ('tatra'). basti is rendered 'bladder'; the sense (bladder or lower abdomen) is not certain. makkalla is a standard name of a post-partum pain with a hard lump in the lower abdomen (usually); this is not in the text and is not added.

words.gloss: yava (barley); kṣāra (an ash-derived salt, standard: crude potassium carbonate, probable); powder

hindi: उसमें यवक्षार यानी सम्भवतः यव के पौधे की राख से बने अशुद्ध पोटैशियम कार्बोनेट का चूर्ण घी के साथ, या सुखोष्ण जल के साथ पीना चाहिए।
english: In that case one should drink the powder of yavakṣāra (kṣāra of barley; probably impure potassium carbonate) with ghee, or with pleasantly warm water.
notes: GROUPING: this is the apodosis of 109 ('tatra'). kṣāra is kept (glossary). The modern identification of yavakṣāra as an impure potassium carbonate from barley plant ash is probable, not certain. The 'or' joins the two vehicles (ghee, warm water). 'pibeta' is the middle optative of √pā.
lines_deva: तत्र यवक्षारचूर्णं सर्पिषा सुखोष्णोदकेन वा पिबेत
lines_iast: tatra yavakṣāracūrṇaṃ sarpiṣā sukhoṣṇodakena vā pibeta

words.gloss: the group beginning with varaṇa (Crateva nurvala; standard)
with pañcakola (the five pungents: long pepper, its root, cavya, citraka, dry ginger; standard)
the group beginning with vīratara; the group beginning with mūṣaka; added substance (pratīvāpa)

hindi: या वरणादि गण को पञ्चकोल यानी पीपर, पीपरामूल, चव्य, चित्रक और सोंठ, एला यानी सम्भवतः इलायची और अस्पष्ट शब्द अतीवाप के साथ। अथवा जिसमें प्रतीवाप यानी मिलाई जाने वाली वस्तु के रूप में वीरतर आदि वाला गण और मूषक आदि वाला गण हों।
english: Or the group beginning with varaṇa, together with pañcakola (long pepper, its root, cavya, citraka and dry ginger), elā (probably cardamom) and atīvāpa (unclear). Or else (one) having as pratīvāpa (added substance) the groups beginning with vīratara and beginning with mūṣaka.

text_flags.why: possible: 'atīvāpa' is not a known word; unit 112 has 'pratīvāpa' (an added substance), so 'ati' may stand for 'prati'; the printed form is kept unsplit as unclear and not adopted

notes: [02.03.111] Split of 'melām' = m (from -am) + elām is a sandhi of -am + elām; read as 'pañcakolam elām'. The syntax is uncertain (elā may be an addition or a separate item). Verb carried from 110: pibet. REVIEW: alternative reading of 'elāmatīvāpaṃ' = elā-pratīvāpam ('with elā as the added substance'), pra misprinted as ma, matching pratīvāpa in 112. Not adopted. [02.03.112] The compound is open: it can be one item 'vīratarādi' taken with 'mūṣakādi as added substance', or both groups as added substances; the literal compound is kept. Members of both groups are not given here. Elliptical: the main substance and the verb are carried from 110-111. REVIEW: 'mūṣaka' may be a misprint of muṣkaka (muṣkakādi is a known drug group named together with vīratarādi); not adopted.

words.gloss: the group beginning with vatsaka; decoction (niryūha)

hindi: या लवण का चूर्ण वत्सक आदि के क्वाथ के साथ।
english: Or salt powder with a decoction (niryūha) of the group beginning with vatsaka.

text_flags.why: possible: vā printed joined without a space

notes: Elliptical: verb carried. Which salt (lavaṇa) is meant is not stated.

hindi: या वत्सक आदि गण को मदिरा के साथ।
english: Or the group beginning with vatsaka, with madirā (an intoxicating drink).
notes: Elliptical: verb carried.

words.gloss: aṃśumatī pair (probably śālaparṇī, Desmodium gangeticum, and pṛśniparṇī, Uraria picta; disputed); decoction
marica (black pepper); bhadradāru (deodar, Cedrus deodara; probable); paste

hindi: या अंशुमती द्वय के काढ़े के साथ, या मरिच और भद्रदारु का कल्क। अंशुमती द्वय यानी सम्भवतः शालपर्णी और पृश्निपर्णी, पहचान विवादित।
english: Or with a decoction of the aṃśumatī pair (probably two plants, śālaparṇī and pṛśniparṇī; identity disputed), or a paste (kalka) of marica (black pepper) and bhadradāru (deodar).

text_flags.why: possible: vā printed joined without a space

notes: 'kaṣāyenavā' is printed joined (kaṣāyena + vā). Elliptical: the main substance and verb come from 110. The two plants of the aṃśumatī pair are an interpretation, not stated in the text (disputed). bhadradāru = deodar is probable. REVIEW: because 'vā' follows kaṣāyena (unlike the 'X vā' pattern of 94-116), the alternative 'paste of marica and bhadradāru with the decoction of the aṃśumatī pair as vehicle' is also possible; the printed order is kept in the translation.

hindi: या अस्पष्ट शब्द भाईीं, नागर यानी सोंठ और देवदारु का कल्क गरम पानी के साथ।
english: Or a paste (kalka) of bhāīīṃ (unclear), nāgara (dry ginger) and devadāru (deodar), with warm water.

text_flags.why: possible: 'bhāīīṃ' is not a word; a damaged 'bhārṅgī' (a plant name) is a guess only and is not adopted

notes: Unrestorable: bhāīīṃ is kept unsplit as unclear; the rest of the compound is translated as a list. Elliptical: the verb is carried.

words.gloss: trikaṭu (the three pungents: dry ginger, black pepper, long pepper; standard)
trijātaka (the three aromatics: cinnamon bark, cardamom, bay-leaf; standard)

hindi: या पुराने गुड़ को त्रिकटु यानी सोंठ, मरिच और पीपर, त्रिजातक यानी दालचीनी, इलायची और तेजपात, और धनिका यानी सम्भवतः धनिया के चूर्ण में मिलाकर खाना चाहिए।
english: Or one should eat old jaggery (guḍa) mixed with the powder of trikaṭu, trijātaka and dhanikā (probably coriander).
notes: The compound 'trikaṭu-trijātaka-dhanikā-cūrṇa' is read as a dvandva of three followed by cūrṇa (one powder). dhanikā: the usual spelling is dhānyaka; coriander is probable. 'Old' for purāṇa (see glossary: jīrṇa 'old').

hindi: यदि उसकी योनि अपने स्थान से खिसक जाए।
english: If her yoni (female genital passage) should slip from its own place.
notes: GROUPING: protasis; the apodosis is in 119 ('tataḥ'). The grammar leaves open whether 'tasyāḥ' is the woman of 109-117. REVIEW: modern equivalent (probable, not stated in the text): prolapse of the genital passage/uterus (yoni-bhraṃśa).

hindi: फिर जिस किसी के भी रक्त से योनि को चुपड़कर कुशल स्त्री उसे यथास्थान बैठा दे।
english: Then, having anointed the yoni with the blood of anyone whatever, a skilled woman should place it back in its proper place.
notes: 'yasya kasyacit' is read as 'of anyone whatever' (an indefinite expression); the animal or person is not stated. 'yasya' and 'kasyacit' are listed as two pronoun words but form one indefinite expression. Hindi 'उसे' stands for the yoni, the object of niveśayet.
lines_deva: ततो यस्य कस्यचिच्छोणितेनाभ्यज्ययोनिं यथास्थानं कुशला स्त्री निवेशयेत्
lines_iast: tato yasya kasyacicchoṇitenābhyajyayoniṃ yathāsthānaṃ kuśalā strī niveśayet

hindi: और स्थापित की गई को अशोक, रोहिणी, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, बर्हिष, जिसकी पहचान अज्ञात है, उशीर यानी खस, प्रियङ्गु यानी सम्भवतः फूलप्रियंगु, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, और देवदारु के कल्क से भली प्रकार पकाए तेल से बार-बार स्वेदन करना चाहिए और भरना चाहिए।
english: And the placed (one) should be fomented many times with oil well cooked with a paste of aśoka, rohiṇī (identity disputed), barhiṣa (unidentified), uśīra, priyaṅgu (probably Callicarpa macrophylla; identity disputed) and devadāru, and filled.

text_flags.why: possible: two words printed joined without a space

notes: 'niviṣṭām' is feminine and agrees with yoni of 119. 'barhiṣa' follows the printed 'barhiṣośīra' (a + u = o); a different division is possible and the plant is not identified here. priyaṅgu is disputed in lists. The verb svedayet (should foment) with oil is as printed; no instrument is added. Object of pūrayet (fill) is not stated, and none is supplied. REVIEW: 'tailena' may govern pūrayet (fill with the oil) rather than, or as well as, svedayet; the translation keeps the printed order.

hindi: और कहना चाहिए: हे सुभगे, अपने स्थान को जाओ।
english: And one should say: "Go, O fortunate one, to your own place."
notes: The closing 'iti' marks the end of the quotation. The speaker and the one addressed (probably the yoni; not stated) are not given.

words.gloss: for the care of a child

hindi: उसी प्रकार कोई एक स्त्री, अभी जन्मे हुए बालक को, बालक के उपचार की विधि से, अनुमानित पाठ पर उत्पन्न करे।
english: In the same way any one woman should bring forth (on a conjectural reading) the child just born, by the procedure for the care of a child.

text_flags.why: possible: strī and jātamātram are printed as one word
possible: th for dh in 'vithinā' and pp for tp; the reading 'utpādayet' is conjectural (upacaret or similar is also possible)

notes: The verb is damaged. The reading 'utpādayet' is a guess; the translations say so. 'anyatamā' is read 'any one (woman)' (anyatama = one of several, not 'other'). 'strījātamātram' read as strī + jātamātram; the alternative 'born of a woman only' is possible.

words.gram: 3 sg. fut. mid. upa-√diś (active sense "will teach", or passive; tam acc. is irregular for a passive)

hindi: उसका उपदेश तो आगे वालों में किया जाएगा।
english: But that will be taught in the later (ones).
notes: 'uttareṣu' is read as 'in the later (ones)', probably the later sthānas (especially Uttarasthāna); this is an interpretation, not stated. 'tam' (masculine) may refer to the procedure (vidhi) or the child.

words.gloss: woman who has recently given birth (sūtikā)
balā (probably country mallow, Sida cordifolia); oil

hindi: फिर प्रसूता यानी सूतिका को बला यानी सम्भवतः बरियार के तेल से अभ्यंग करना चाहिए।
english: Then one should anoint the sūtikā (woman who has recently given birth) with balā-oil (balā: probably country mallow).
notes: balā = Sida cordifolia is probable (several plants are called balā). Hindi: abhyañj is rendered 'अभ्यंग' (anointing with oil).

hindi: और भूखी को पञ्चकोल के चूर्ण से, या यवानी यानी अजवायन, उपकुञ्चिका यानी सम्भवतः कलौंजी, जिसकी पहचान विवादित है, चव्य, चित्रक, व्योष और सैन्धव यानी सेंधा नमक के चूर्ण से युक्त, दिन में पचने वाली स्नेह की मात्रा, सात्म्य के अनुसार, पिलानी चाहिए।
english: And a dose (mātrā) of sneha (oil or fat), joined with pañcakola powder, or with the powder of yavānī (ajwain), upakuñcikā (probably nigella; identity disputed), cavya, citraka, vyoṣa and saindhava (rock salt), digesting within the day, should be given to the hungry (one) to drink, according to suitability (sātmya).

text_flags.why: possible: ca printed joined without a space

notes: The 'vā' sits between the two powders: 'with pañcakola powder, or with powder of ...'. 'ahaḥpariṇāminīm' is read 'digesting within the day'; the dose that is digested by the day's end is a standard reading but not stated. 'ca' at the start is read as joining this to 124.
lines_deva: बुभुक्षितां चपंचकोलचूर्णेन यवान्युपकुंचिकाचव्यचित्रकव्योषसैंधवचूर्णेन वा युक्तामहःपरिणामिनीं यथासात्म्यं स्नेहमात्रां पाययेत्
lines_iast: bubhukṣitāṃ capaṃcakolacūrṇena yavānyupakuṃcikācavyacitrakavyoṣasaiṃdhavacūrṇena vā yuktāmahaḥpariṇāminīṃ yathāsātmyaṃ snehamātrāṃ pāyayet

words.gloss: lesser; pañcamūla (group of five roots); decoction
with yamaka (a mixture of two fats, probably oil and ghee)

hindi: स्नेह के अयोग्य को वात हरने वाली औषधियों का क्वाथ, या ह्रस्व पञ्चमूल यानी छोटी पाँच जड़ों, शालपर्णी, पृश्निपर्णी, बृहती, कण्टकारी और गोक्षुर, का क्वाथ; और जिसने पी लिया हो उसके पेट पर यमक यानी सम्भवतः तेल और घी के मिश्रण से अभ्यंग करके कपड़े से लपेटना चाहिए।
english: For one unfit for sneha (oil or fat), a decoction of vāta-relieving medicines, or a decoction of the lesser pañcamūla (the five small roots: śālaparṇī, pṛśniparṇī, bṛhatī, kaṇṭakārī and gokṣura); and for one who has drunk, having anointed with yamaka (probably a mixture of oil and ghee), one should wrap the belly with cloth.

text_flags.why: possible: 'katha' for 'kvātha' (decoction); the same print habit is seen in 128 (kathātha) and 131 (kathita)
possible: stray '=' sign printed before the word; 'katha' for 'kvātha' as above

notes: Elliptical: the verb of the first clause is carried from 125 (pāyayet) and none is supplied. yamaka (the two-fat mixture) is standard in the tradition but not stated here: probable. The lesser pañcamūla (laghu pañcamūla) is the group of five smaller roots (standard); the text only says hrasva. 'kvātha' for 'katha' is read as a print habit; recorded once here.
lines_deva: स्नेहायोग्यां वातहरौषधकथं =ह्रस्वपंचमूलकथं वा पीतवत्याश्च यमकेनाभ्यज्य वेष्टयेदुदरं वस्त्रेण
lines_iast: snehāyogyāṃ vātaharauṣadhakathaṃ =hrasvapaṃcamūlakathaṃ vā pītavatyāśca yamakenābhyajya veṣṭayedudaraṃ vastreṇa

hindi: इस प्रकार वायु उदर के विकार को उत्पन्न नहीं करेगी, अवकाश न होने के कारण।
english: Thus wind (vāyu) would not produce an alteration of the belly (udara), because of the absence of space.

text_flags.why: possible: 'vikkṛti' for 'vikṛti' (doubled k)

notes: 'udara' is rendered 'belly' (glossary), so the alteration is of the belly, not the disease udara. The optative is read as a potential ('would').

words.gloss: vidārī (Pueraria tuberosa; probable); the group beginning with; decoction

hindi: स्नेह के पच जाने पर पहले वाली ही औषधियों से पकाई हुई, या विदारी आदि गण के क्वाथ से, या दूध से पकाई हुई, भली प्रकार उबाली हुई, तरल यवागू मात्रा से पिलानी चाहिए।
english: But when the sneha has been digested, a yavāgū (gruel) cooked with the very same earlier medicines, or with a decoction of the group beginning with vidārī, or with milk, well boiled and liquid, should be given to drink in measure.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kathātha' for 'kvātha' (decoction); print habit seen in 126

notes: jīrṇa here is 'digested' (of the sneha). 'siddhām' (cooked) is read as governing all three means (earlier medicines, decoction, milk); 'susvinnām dravām' = well boiled and liquid. vidārī = Pueraria tuberosa is probable (several plants are called vidārī). 'mātrayā' = in measure (a proper dose).
lines_deva: जीर्णे तु स्नेहे पूर्वौषधैरेव सिद्धां विदार्यादिगणकथाथेन क्षीरेण वा यवागूं सुस्विन्नां द्रवां मात्रया पाययेत्
lines_iast: jīrṇe tu snehe pūrvauṣadhaireva siddhāṃ vidāryādigaṇakathāthena kṣīreṇa vā yavāgūṃ susvinnāṃ dravāṃ mātrayā pāyayet

words.gloss: of the drinking of sneha and yavāgū

hindi: और स्नेह और यवागू के पीने से पहले, दोनों समय गरम पानी से सींचना चाहिए।
english: And before the drinking of sneha and of yavāgū, at both times, one should sprinkle with hot water.

text_flags.why: possible: short a printed for ā in 'pānābhyām' (ablative dual after prāk)

notes: The object (the body, or the woman) is not stated and none is supplied. 'ubhayakālam' is read as 'at both times' (before the sneha and before the yavāgū). pariṣecana is a sprinkling or bathing with liquid.

words.gloss: jāṅgala (flesh of dry-land animals; standard); broths; and so on
digestive fire, strength and the rest

hindi: इस प्रकार तीन रात, पाँच रात या अस्पष्ट शब्द समरात्र निभाकर, फिर यव, कोल यानी बेर और कुलत्थ यानी कुलथी के यूष से और हल्के अन्न-पान से, और बारह रात के बाद जाङ्गल यानी सूखे प्रदेश के पशुओं के रस आदि से क्रम से पोषण करना चाहिए, अग्नि, बल आदि को देखकर।
english: Having kept this up for three nights, five nights, or samarātra (unclear), one should then nourish (her) gradually with a soup (yūṣa) of barley, jujube (kola) and horse gram (kulattha), with light food and drink, and after twelve nights with jāṅgala broths and the like, having regard to the digestive fire (agni), strength and so on.

text_flags.why: possible: 'sama' is not a natural number word here; the OCR confusion pta/ma is known in this print; the printed form is kept and the reading 'seven nights' is not adopted
possible: two words printed joined without a space

notes: The object of āpyāyet is not stated; (her) is shown in brackets in English only. 'jāṅgala' is read as an adjective (of dry-land animals) used as a noun for their flesh; broths of it. The 'ca' after jāṅgalarasādibhiḥ joins it to the earlier soup. 'agnibalādīni' = agni, bala and the rest. The sandhi 'anupālya' after vā' follows the print.
lines_deva: एवं त्रिरात्रंपंचरात्रं समरात्रं वाऽनुपाल्य ततो यवकोलकुलत्थयूषेण लघुनाचान्नपानेन द्वादशरात्रात्परं जांगलरसादिभिश्च क्रमादाप्यायेदग्निबलादीन्यपेक्ष्य
lines_iast: evaṃ trirātraṃpaṃcarātraṃ samarātraṃ vā'nupālya tato yavakolakulatthayūṣeṇa laghunācānnapānena dvādaśarātrātparaṃ jāṃgalarasādibhiśca kramādāpyāyedagnibalādīnyapekṣya

hindi: और उबालकर ठण्डा किया हुआ पानी पिलाना चाहिए।
english: And water that has been boiled and cooled should be given to drink.

text_flags.why: possible: 'kathita' (said) for 'kvathita' (boiled); the same print habit as 'katha' for 'kvātha' in 126

notes: The reading 'boiled' for kathita rests on the sense (boiled and cooled water); 'said' would not fit.

words.gloss: (ones) cooked with life-promoting (jīvanīya), nourishing (bṛṃhaṇīya), sweet and vāta-relieving (drugs)

hindi: इसी प्रकार जीवनीय, बृंहणीय, मधुर और वात हरने वालों से सिद्ध किए हुओं से अभ्यंग, अस्पष्ट शब्द उच्छादन, परिषेक और अवगाहन से, और हृदय को प्रिय अन्न-पान से उपचार करना चाहिए।
english: Likewise one should attend (to her) with (ones) cooked with life-promoting (jīvanīya), nourishing (bṛṃhaṇīya), sweet and vāta-relieving (ones), through anointing (abhyaṅga), ucchādana (unclear), sprinkling (pariṣeka) and immersion (avagāha), and with agreeable foods and drinks.

text_flags.why: possible: 'hra' printed for 'hṛ'
possible: 'ucchādana' is not a clear word here; 'utsādana' (rubbing) or another is a guess only

notes: The sandhi runs across the printed gap: 'avagāhai' + 'rannapānaiśca' = avagāhaiḥ + annapānaiḥ ca. jīvanīya and bṛṃhaṇīya are named groups of drugs (standard: life-promoting and nourishing groups), here as a compound with 'sweet' and 'vāta-relieving'. The compound is read with siddha as the last member of one expression. 'hṛdya' = pleasant (lit. 'of the heart'); the English does not say 'heart'. The object (her) is not stated.

words.gloss: of the sūtikā (woman who has recently given birth)

hindi: क्योंकि इस प्रकार, अनुमानित पाठ पर, गर्भ की वृद्धि से क्षीण और शिथिल हुए सारे शरीर के धातुओं वाले, और अस्पष्ट शब्द प्रवाहुण, वेदना, क्लेद और विशेष रूप से रक्त के निकलने से रिक्त शरीर से, वह फिर नई हो जाती है। इसी कारण सूतिका का रोग कष्टसाध्य या असाध्य होता है। इसलिए उसका यथोक्त विधि से प्रयत्न पूर्वक उपचार करना चाहिए।
english: For thus, on a conjectural reading, from the body whose dhātus of the whole body have been wasted (kṣapita) and made slack (śithila) by the growth of the foetus, and which is emptied of pravāhuṇa (unclear), pain, moisture (kleda), the outflow of blood, in particular, (she) becomes new again. And for this very reason the disease of the sūtikā becomes hard to cure or incurable. Therefore she should be treated with effort by the procedure as stated.

text_flags.why: possible: stray anusvāra in 'vṛddhiṃ'; 'pravāhuṇa' is unclear (perhaps 'pravāhaṇa', straining) and the compound is joined with 'ca' without a space
possible: two words printed joined without a space

notes: The long compound is hard and the division is conjectural; the translations say so. 'pravāhuṇa' is unclear (perhaps pravāhaṇa 'bearing down'; not adopted). The reading 'wasted and slack by the growth of the foetus' takes garbhavṛddhi as the cause; 'viśeṣa' is taken as 'in particular' attached to the blood-outflow. 'punarnavī' is a cvi formation (becomes new again). 'ataeva' = atas eva. The disease of the sūtikā is not named. REVIEW: alternative sense of '-śūnya-śarīrāt': 'from the body depleted by (the effects of) bearing-down, pain, discharge and blood-flow'; the draft's 'emptied of' is only one reading.
lines_deva: एवं हि गर्भवृद्धिंक्षपितशिथिलसर्वशरीरधातुप्रवाहुणवेदनाक्लेदरक्तनिस्रुतविशेषशून्यशरीराच्च पुनर्नवीभवत्यतएव च सूतिकाया व्याधिः कृच्छ्रसाध्यो भवत्यसाध्यो वा तस्मात्तां यथोक्तेनविधिना प्रयत्नेनोपचरेत्
lines_iast: evaṃ hi garbhavṛddhiṃkṣapitaśithilasarvaśarīradhātupravāhuṇavedanākledaraktanisrutaviśeṣaśūnyaśarīrācca punarnavībhavatyataeva ca sūtikāyā vyādhiḥ kṛcchrasādhyo bhavatyasādhyo vā tasmāttāṃ yathoktenavidhinā prayatnenopacaret

words.gloss: for one and a half months
released from the restraint of food and conduct
one from whom the name sūtikā has gone

hindi: इस प्रकार डेढ़ मास तक उपचारित की गई, क्रम से आहार और विहार के नियन्त्रण से मुक्त हुई, वह ऐसी हो जाए कि उसका सूतिका नाम चला गया हो।
english: Thus, treated for one and a half months and gradually released from the restraint of food and conduct, she would be one from whom the name sūtikā has gone.

text_flags.why: possible: anusvāra printed for the short 'a' of vigata (gone); sense and the usual form vigata fit
possible: words printed joined without a space and hiatus 'vimuktaāhāra' unusual; ablative -āt lost is only a guess

notes: Orthographic notes: doubled -rdd- in adhyarddha is normalised to -rdh- and yaṃtraṇā to yantraṇā (print habit, recorded once). 'vimukta-āhāra-vihāra-yantraṇā' is read as one bahuvrīhi; the alternative 'vimuktā' (she, freed) with 'āhāra-vihāra-yantraṇā' (restraint of food and conduct) as a separate word is possible. 'adhyardha' = one and a half (a half added to a whole). 'syāt' is read 'would be'.

hindi: आर्तव यानी रज के फिर दिखने से, ऐसा कुछ लोगों का मत है।
english: From the reappearance of the ārtava (menses), so some (say).
notes: Doubled -rtt- in ārttava is normalised to ārtava (print habit). 'iti eke' = 'so some (say)'; the verb is not in the text. The ablative can mean 'after' or 'at the time of' the reappearance; the literal 'from' is kept. The unit appears to continue 134 (the end of the period of the sūtikā), as a variant view.

hindi: इस प्रकार प्रथम मास को लेकर, जब तक वह फिर गर्भ के योग्य न हो। स्त्री हो; तब तक सारी विधि सब प्रकार से भली भाँति दिखाई गई है।
english: Thus, taking the first month, as long as (she) is again capable of a foetus (garbha). The woman would be (so); until then the whole procedure has been shown well in every way.
notes: [02.03.136] GROUPING: the 'yāvat' clause appears to continue in 137 ('tāvat'): the two printed lines appear to form one sentence. The metre (8 + 8 syllables in 136 and again in 137) fits this. 'iti' is kept as 'thus'. 'ādāya' = taking (as the start), so 'from the first month onward' is the sense; the translation stays literal. The subject (the woman) comes in 137. [02.03.137] GROUPING: appears to continue 136; the 'yāvat' clause of 136 and 'strī syāt' here read together as 'as long as the woman is again capable of a foetus'. The translation keeps the lines separate. 'tāvat' is the correlative of 'yāvat' in 136.

words.gloss: Garbhopacaraṇīya (the care to be given in pregnancy)

hindi: इस प्रकार गर्भोपचरणीय नामक तीसरा अध्याय।
english: Thus the third chapter, named Garbhopacaraṇīya.
notes: Colophon. 'Garbhopacaraṇīya' is kept as the chapter title; it can mean what is to be done for (the woman with) the foetus, that is, care of pregnancy and its aftermath; it is not translated as a fixed phrase. The printed 'nāmatṛtīyo'dhyāyaḥ' is nāma + tṛtīyaḥ + adhyāyaḥ with the avagraha.
